cases.name: case101_prim_onehot_multihot_suppressed
cases.bug_type: multihot error suppressed
cases.spec: When more than one bit of oh_i is high in the same cycle, err_o must assert in that same cycle.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (((((oh_i == 4'b1010) && ($past(oh_i) == 4'b1010)) || ((oh_i == 4'b1100) && ($past(oh_i) == 4'b1100))) && en_i && $past(en_i))) |-> err_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: A multihot onehot vector must trigger err_o in the sampled cycle.

loose_negative_controls.name: enable_only
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!en_i) |-> !err_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It constrains only the disabled case and says nothing about multihot inputs while enabled.

loose_negative_controls.name: eventual_error
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (|oh_i) |-> (err_o || en_i));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It is too weak and does not require exact multihot detection.

cases.hard_case_rationale: A vague assertion like 'onehot input should be legal' can pass without explicitly checking the multihot corner. The precise bug appears only when two request bits are simultaneously high.
cases.stimulus_notes: Drive legal onehot patterns first, then inject 4'b1010 and 4'b0110 while en_i is high. Held-out should use different multihot literals.

cases.name: case102_prim_onehot_enable_mismatch_suppressed
cases.bug_type: enable mismatch error suppressed
cases.spec: With strict enable checking enabled, err_o shall assert whenever en_i disagrees with whether any onehot bit is set.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (((oh_i == 4'b0000) && ($past(oh_i) == 4'b0000) && en_i && $past(en_i))) |-> err_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: The checker must flag disagreement between en_i and the OR-reduced oh_i input.

loose_negative_controls.name: multihot_only
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It ignores the legal onehot-but-disabled and zero-hot-but-enabled mismatches.

loose_negative_controls.name: request_implies_enable
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (|oh_i) |-> en_i);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It checks only one direction and misses the all-zero while enabled corner.

cases.hard_case_rationale: The mutation does not break basic onehot structure. Only an assertion that ties en_i exactly to the presence of a selected bit can expose it.
cases.stimulus_notes: Use both mismatch directions: oh_i=0 with en_i=1, and oh_i=4'b0100 with en_i=0. Held-out should use different onehot positions.

cases.name: case103_prim_onehot_addr_mismatch_suppressed
cases.bug_type: address mismatch error suppressed
cases.spec: If exactly one bit of oh_i is high, err_o shall assert when addr_i points to a different bit in the same cycle.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (((((oh_i == 4'b0100) && ($past(oh_i) == 4'b0100) && (addr_i == 2'd0) && ($past(addr_i) == 2'd0)) || ((oh_i == 4'b0010) && ($past(oh_i) == 4'b0010) && (addr_i == 2'd0) && ($past(addr_i) == 2'd0))) && en_i && $past(en_i))) |-> err_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: A onehot vector whose active bit disagrees with addr_i must be rejected immediately.

loose_negative_controls.name: enable_consistency_only
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (((|oh_i) ^ en_i)) |-> err_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: en_i can still match |oh_i| even when addr_i points to the wrong position.

loose_negative_controls.name: any_request_valid
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (|oh_i) |-> !err_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It treats any asserted onehot vector as valid and therefore misses the index mismatch.

cases.hard_case_rationale: The bug is not about onehotness; it is about exact bit-to-index consistency. General 'onehot legal' assertions will miss it.
cases.stimulus_notes: Hold oh_i onehot while sweeping addr_i across both matching and mismatching values. Held-out should use different active bits.

cases.name: case104_prim_fifo_full_early
cases.bug_type: full asserted one slot early
cases.spec: full_o shall assert if and only if the FIFO currently contains Depth entries; it must remain low at Depth-1.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) ((wptr_o == 2'd3) && !incr_rptr_i && !empty_o && !clr_i) |-> !full_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: At the last legal pre-wrap write pointer position, the FIFO is not yet full and full_o must remain low.

loose_negative_controls.name: full_implies_max_depth
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) full_o |-> (depth_o == 3'd4));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It may stay vacuous if the bug avoids asserting full under the sampled corner or if the depth output is also misleading.

loose_negative_controls.name: eventual_full_after_writes
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) incr_wptr_i |-> !empty_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It does not constrain the exact boundary cycle where full must remain low.

cases.hard_case_rationale: This is a classic tight boundary bug. A hand-wavy FIFO assertion can pass while missing the exact Depth-1 cycle.
cases.overfit_lure: Use Depth=4 and primary trace values 0,1,2,3,4 so trace-informed methods are tempted to memorize the literal boundary.
cases.stimulus_notes: Fill the FIFO to 3 entries without reads, sample full_o at depth 3, then push once more. Held-out should use an interleaved read/write prelude before reaching depth 3 again.

cases.name: case105_prim_fifo_empty_late
cases.bug_type: empty asserted one cycle late
cases.spec: empty_o shall assert in the same cycle the FIFO occupancy returns to zero.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (depth_o == 3'd0) |-> empty_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: Whenever occupancy is zero, empty_o must be high immediately.

loose_negative_controls.name: empty_after_clear_only
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) clr_i |=> empty_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It checks reset-like clearing but not the normal read-to-empty transition.

loose_negative_controls.name: no_full_when_empty
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) empty_o |-> !full_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The buggy design can satisfy this while still delaying empty_o.

cases.hard_case_rationale: The bug only appears at the exact zero-occupancy return point. Loose assertions about mutual exclusion of full/empty are not enough.
cases.overfit_lure: Use explicit depth values 2,1,0 in the primary trace so a trace-guided model can be baited into literal matching.
cases.stimulus_notes: Write two entries, read them out, and sample the final read-to-empty transition. Held-out should empty after a write/read/write/read pattern.

cases.name: case106_prim_fifo_depth_off_by_one
cases.bug_type: depth output biased high by one
cases.spec: depth_o shall equal the exact FIFO occupancy in every cycle.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (empty_o) |-> (depth_o == 3'd0));
golden_sva.expected_behavior: When the FIFO is empty, the occupancy output must report zero rather than a biased nonzero value.

loose_negative_controls.name: write_makes_fifo_nonempty
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (incr_wptr_i && !incr_rptr_i && !clr_i) |-> !empty_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: A depth output biased high by one can still leave the empty flag behavior looking reasonable after writes.

loose_negative_controls.name: full_empty_exclusive
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) !(full_o && empty_o));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It ignores the numeric correctness of depth_o itself.

cases.hard_case_rationale: This bug is subtle because the control flags can look mostly plausible. Only a precise occupancy relation catches it.
cases.stimulus_notes: Exercise empty, single-entry, and two-entry states. Held-out should revisit zero occupancy after a clear pulse.

cases.name: case110_prim_intr_event_overwrite
cases.bug_type: event state overwrite instead of hold-until-clear
cases.spec: For Event interrupts, once a new event sets the interrupt state, the state shall remain set across subsequent cycles until software clears it.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) ($past(reg2hw_intr_state_q_i) && reg2hw_intr_state_q_i && reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i) |-> intr_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: Once event state is latched and remains high, the enabled interrupt output must stay asserted on the next sampled cycle.

loose_negative_controls.name: state_update_flag_matches_data
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) hw2reg_intr_state_de_o |-> hw2reg_intr_state_d_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It only checks that the CSR update path drives a high state when the update flag is asserted, not that the enabled interrupt remains visible afterward.

loose_negative_controls.name: masked_interrupt_low
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i) |-> !intr_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The bug is about losing a latched enabled interrupt, not masked behavior.

cases.hard_case_rationale: This is exactly the kind of hold-state bug that vague 'event causes interrupt' assertions miss. The state is set once, then silently forgotten.
cases.stimulus_notes: Model the CSR state feedback in tb, set an event, idle without clearing, and confirm state persistence. Held-out should insert a test pulse before the persistent hold check.

cases.name: case111_prim_intr_output_or_mask
cases.bug_type: interrupt enable mask turned into OR
cases.spec: The outgoing interrupt shall assert only when both the interrupt status and enable are high.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i && !$past(reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i) && reg2hw_intr_state_q_i && $past(reg2hw_intr_state_q_i)) |-> !intr_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: Masking the interrupt must suppress intr_o regardless of stored status.

loose_negative_controls.name: event_implies_event_detect
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) event_intr_i |-> hw2reg_intr_state_de_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It ignores the mask/output relation entirely.

loose_negative_controls.name: status_can_raise_interrupt
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i && $past(reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i) && reg2hw_intr_state_q_i && $past(reg2hw_intr_state_q_i)) |-> intr_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It checks only the enabled visibility case and ignores the masked-state corner where the OR bug leaks through.

cases.hard_case_rationale: The internal event machinery can still look healthy while the externally visible mask logic is wrong.
cases.stimulus_notes: Keep reg2hw_intr_state_q_i high while toggling enable. Held-out should build status via event feedback first, then mask it.

cases.name: case112_prim_intr_test_pulse_dropped
cases.bug_type: interrupt test write pulse is lost
cases.spec: In Status mode, a software test pulse written through reg2hw_intr_test_qe_i shall be captured and reflected in the stored test_q state on the next cycle.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (reg2hw_intr_test_qe_i && $past(reg2hw_intr_test_qe_i) && reg2hw_intr_test_q_i && $past(reg2hw_intr_test_q_i) && reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i && $past(reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i)) |-> hw2reg_intr_state_d_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: A test write must drive the next-state interrupt bit high immediately so the pulse is captured on the following cycle.

loose_negative_controls.name: event_path_only
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) event_intr_i |-> intr_o || !intr_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It ignores the software-injected test path completely.

loose_negative_controls.name: qe_seen
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) reg2hw_intr_test_qe_i |-> reg2hw_intr_test_qe_i);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It is vacuous and does not check the captured effect.

cases.hard_case_rationale: The test path is easy to overlook if assertions focus only on hardware events.
cases.stimulus_notes: Instantiate Status mode, enable the interrupt, pulse reg2hw_intr_test_qe_i for one cycle, and watch the next-cycle output. Held-out should combine a test pulse with inactive event_intr_i.

cases.name: case113_prim_edge_posedge_misdecoded
cases.bug_type: posedge output decodes negedge
cases.spec: q_posedge_pulse_o shall pulse for exactly the sampled 0->1 transition and not for 1->0 transitions.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!$past(q_sync_o) && q_sync_o) |-> q_posedge_pulse_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: A sampled rising input edge must create a posedge pulse rather than a negedge pulse.

loose_negative_controls.name: some_event_on_change
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (d_i != q_sync_o) |-> (q_posedge_pulse_o || q_negedge_pulse_o));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The buggy design still produces an event pulse, just on the wrong output.

loose_negative_controls.name: pulse_is_onehot
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) !(q_posedge_pulse_o && q_negedge_pulse_o));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: Wrong polarity can still satisfy one-hot pulse exclusivity.

cases.hard_case_rationale: A broad 'signal changes cause a pulse' assertion is too loose; only exact edge polarity catches this mutation.
cases.stimulus_notes: Use EnSync=0 in wrapper and toggle d_i 0->1 and 1->0 on separate cycles. Held-out should repeat with longer high/low runs between edges.

cases.name: case114_prim_edge_negedge_misdecoded
cases.bug_type: negedge output decodes posedge
cases.spec: q_negedge_pulse_o shall pulse for exactly the sampled 1->0 transition and not for 0->1 transitions.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) ($past(d_i) && !d_i) |-> q_negedge_pulse_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: A sampled falling input edge must create a negedge pulse rather than a posedge pulse.

loose_negative_controls.name: event_exists
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (d_i != q_sync_o) |-> (q_posedge_pulse_o || q_negedge_pulse_o));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It ignores which edge output is supposed to fire.

loose_negative_controls.name: stable_no_pulse
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (d_i == q_sync_o) |-> !(q_posedge_pulse_o || q_negedge_pulse_o));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The bug occurs only on transitions, not on stable cycles.

cases.hard_case_rationale: Like the posedge case, this forces exact polarity rather than generic 'edge activity' checking.
cases.stimulus_notes: Toggle d_i through both rising and falling transitions with clean holds in between. Held-out should use a different ordering of edges.

cases.name: case115_prim_edge_both_edges_collapsed
cases.bug_type: posedge output fires on both edges
cases.spec: q_posedge_pulse_o shall remain low on falling edges and assert only on rising edges.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) ($past(d_i) && !d_i) |-> !q_posedge_pulse_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: A falling edge must not leak into the posedge pulse output.

loose_negative_controls.name: pulse_occurs_on_rise
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!q_sync_o && d_i) |-> q_posedge_pulse_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The buggy implementation still pulses on rises; the problem is the extra pulses on falls.

loose_negative_controls.name: negedge_output_correct
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (q_sync_o && !d_i) |-> q_negedge_pulse_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The negedge output can stay correct while the posedge output spuriously fires too.

cases.hard_case_rationale: This is a good 'conservative assertion misses the false positives' case: one can verify positive behavior and still miss illegal extra pulses.
cases.stimulus_notes: Include at least one clean falling edge where only q_negedge_pulse_o should assert. Held-out should vary the time spent high before falling.

cases.name: case116_prim_filter_late_accept
cases.bug_type: filtered output switches one cycle late
cases.spec: With filtering enabled, filter_o shall adopt a new stable input at the exact acceptance boundary, not one sampled cycle later.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) accept_boundary_dbg |-> (filter_o == filter_i));
golden_sva.expected_behavior: Whenever the filter reaches its acceptance boundary while enabled, the sampled output must already equal the new stable input on that same cycle.

loose_negative_controls.name: eventual_switch
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (enable_i && filter_i && $past(filter_o)) |-> filter_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It allows the output to lag by an unspecified amount.

loose_negative_controls.name: steady_input_implies_stable_output
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!enable_i) |-> (filter_o == filter_i));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The bug occurs only while enabled and at the exact threshold boundary.

cases.hard_case_rationale: This is precisely the kind of cross-cycle boundary condition that vague filtering assertions under-specify.
cases.overfit_lure: Use Cycles=3 with trace runs like 000111 so trace methods see tempting literal streaks.
cases.stimulus_notes: With Cycles=2, drive the new value from a negedge so the second agreeing enabled posedge is the exact acceptance boundary. Held-out should first establish the opposite stored polarity, then test the same two-sample boundary in reverse.

cases.name: case117_prim_filter_bypass_stale
cases.bug_type: disabled bypass returns stale filtered state
cases.spec: When enable_i is low, filter_o shall immediately bypass to the current input rather than the stored filtered state.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!enable_i && $past(enable_i) && (filter_i != $past(filter_i)) && ($past(filter_o) == $past(filter_i))) |-> (filter_o == filter_i));
golden_sva.expected_behavior: On the first disabled sampled cycle after a previously tracked value is established, the bypassed output must match the live input immediately.

loose_negative_controls.name: enabled_threshold_only
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (enable_i && filter_o) |-> filter_i);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It only constrains cycles where the enabled path is already outputting high, so it ignores the disabled bypass edge where this bug lives.

loose_negative_controls.name: stored_value_eventual_match
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) filter_o |-> filter_i || $past(filter_i));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It allows stale filtered output to look acceptable.

cases.hard_case_rationale: This is not a basic functionality failure; the filter still behaves plausibly while enabled. The bug hides in the exact bypass semantics.
cases.stimulus_notes: Prime the stored value while enabled, then disable from a negedge and flip filter_i so the first disabled sampled cycle reveals stale-vs-live bypass behavior. Held-out should use the opposite stored polarity.

cases.name: case118_prim_filter_ctr_early_accept
cases.bug_type: counter-based filter accepts one cycle early
cases.spec: With filtering enabled, filter_o shall not switch until thresh_i consecutive agreeing samples have been observed.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) pre_accept_hold_dbg |-> !filter_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: Whenever the counter-based filter is still in its pre-accept hold window, the filtered output must remain at the old value rather than switching early.

loose_negative_controls.name: eventual_accept
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (enable_i && filter_i) |-> (filter_o || !$past(filter_o)));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It allows the switch to happen too soon.

loose_negative_controls.name: disabled_bypass_only
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!enable_i) |-> (filter_o == filter_i));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It says nothing about the threshold timing while enabled.

cases.hard_case_rationale: An 'eventually filters the input' assertion is exactly the wrong abstraction here; the boundary cycle matters.
cases.overfit_lure: Use thresh_i values like 2 and 3 in primary traces to tempt constant pinning.
cases.stimulus_notes: Start from low, drive high for one cycle less than threshold and confirm no switch, then hit threshold. Held-out should exercise a different threshold literal.

cases.name: case119_prim_filter_ctr_late_accept
cases.bug_type: counter-based filter accepts one cycle late
cases.spec: With filtering enabled, filter_o shall switch by the exact threshold cycle rather than lagging by one extra sample.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) accept_boundary_dbg |-> (filter_o == filter_i));
golden_sva.expected_behavior: At the exact threshold boundary, the filtered output must already have switched to the newly accepted input value.

loose_negative_controls.name: two_or_more_highs_eventually_high
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (enable_i && filter_i && $past(filter_o)) |-> filter_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It permits an unspecified extra cycle of latency.

loose_negative_controls.name: no_glitch_when_disabled
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!enable_i) |-> (filter_o == filter_i));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The bug is in enabled threshold timing, not in bypass mode.

cases.hard_case_rationale: This is a clean exact-threshold bug with a natural trace-summary overfit lure around the threshold literal.
cases.overfit_lure: Use primary trace threshold 2 and held-out threshold 3 so literal hard-coding can be detected.
cases.stimulus_notes: Run one case with thresh_i=2 in the prompt trace and another hidden held-out check with thresh_i=3.

cases.name: case120_prim_filter_ctr_bypass_stale
cases.bug_type: counter-based filter bypass returns stale state
cases.spec: When enable_i is low, filter_o shall bypass to the current input rather than stay at the previously stored filtered value.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!enable_i && $past(enable_i) && (filter_i != $past(filter_i)) && ($past(filter_o) == $past(filter_i))) |-> (filter_o == filter_i));
golden_sva.expected_behavior: On the first disabled sampled cycle after a previously tracked value is established, the counter-based bypass must match the live input immediately.

loose_negative_controls.name: enabled_eventual_accept
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (enable_i && filter_o) |-> filter_i);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It checks only cycles where the enabled counter-based path is already driving high and says nothing about the disabled bypass edge.

loose_negative_controls.name: threshold_nonzero
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) enable_i |-> (thresh_i != '0 || thresh_i == '0));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It is effectively unconstrained and misses the bypass bug entirely.

cases.hard_case_rationale: Like the shift-register filter bypass case, this bug hides in control gating rather than headline functionality.
cases.stimulus_notes: Prime the counter-based stored state while enabled, then disable from a negedge and flip filter_i so the first disabled sampled cycle reveals stale-vs-live bypass behavior. Held-out should reverse the stored polarity.

cases.name: case124_prim_fifo_clear_ignored
cases.bug_type: clear pulse does not reset FIFO pointers
cases.spec: A clear pulse shall reset the FIFO occupancy and pointers on the next cycle.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) $past(clr_i) |-> (empty_o && (depth_o == 3'd0) && (wptr_o == 2'd0) && (rptr_o == 2'd0)));
golden_sva.expected_behavior: On the cycle after a sampled clear pulse, the FIFO-visible occupancy and both pointers must be at the reset state.

loose_negative_controls.name: eventual_empty_after_reads
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) incr_rptr_i |-> !full_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: Reads can still eventually drain the FIFO without proving clear works.

loose_negative_controls.name: reset_path_only
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) !rst_n |-> empty_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It checks asynchronous reset rather than operational clear.

cases.hard_case_rationale: The bug hides in an operational control path distinct from reset. Loose FIFO assertions rarely distinguish the two.
cases.stimulus_notes: Fill the FIFO, pulse clr_i, and sample the next cycle. Held-out should clear from a different occupancy level.

cases.name: case125_prim_fifo_wrap_late
cases.bug_type: write pointer wraps one cycle late
cases.spec: When the write pointer is at Depth-1 and a write occurs, the internal write pointer shall wrap on the next cycle rather than stepping to an out-of-range state.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) ($past(full_o) && incr_rptr_i && !$past(clr_i)) |-> (depth_o == 3'd3));
golden_sva.expected_behavior: Reading one item from a full FIFO must reduce occupancy from 4 to 3 on the next sampled cycle.

loose_negative_controls.name: full_implies_not_empty
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) full_o |-> !empty_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The FIFO can still avoid the contradictory full-and-empty state while the post-wrap read depth is corrupted.

loose_negative_controls.name: full_eventually_asserts
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (depth_o == 3'd3 && incr_wptr_i) |-> full_o || $past(full_o));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It does not require the exact pointer wrap relation.

cases.hard_case_rationale: Boundary pointer semantics are much tighter than generic occupancy checks.
cases.overfit_lure: Use visible pointer sequence 0,1,2,3,0 in the primary trace and a different prelude in held-out.
cases.stimulus_notes: Drive four writes from reset and sample wptr_o at the wrap. Held-out should include a read before the final wrap sequence.

cases.name: case126_prim_regwe_enable_gap

golden_sva.expected_behavior: A sustained nonzero write-enable vector must be rejected whenever the enable gate is low, regardless of which onehot bit is active.

loose_negative_controls.name: multihot_only
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: A legal onehot vector with en_i low is still illegal for this module but passes this looser check.

loose_negative_controls.name: zero_ok_when_disabled
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!en_i && !(|oh_i)) |-> !err_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It only checks the easy disabled-zero corner.

cases.hard_case_rationale: This module is a good same-cycle 'context matters' case: onehot legality alone is not enough; enable gating is part of correctness.
cases.stimulus_notes: Drive legal onehot oh_i values while toggling en_i low. Held-out should use different bit positions and include an all-zero disabled control sample.

cases.name: case128_prim_intr_event_mask_stall
cases.bug_type: flopped interrupt output exposes pending next-state before committed state feedback

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (event_intr_i && reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i && !reg2hw_intr_state_q_i) |=> !intr_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: Immediately after a fresh event, the flopped output must still remain low until the committed state feedback has caught up.

loose_negative_controls.name: event_updates_state
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) event_intr_i |-> hw2reg_intr_state_de_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The state-update side can still behave correctly even if the flopped output reads the wrong source too early.

loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i) |-> !intr_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The bug occurs while enabled, as an early visible pulse, not as masked suppression.

cases.hard_case_rationale: This is a source-alignment timing bug: broad assertions about eventual interrupt visibility or state update still pass, but an exact committed-state contract catches it.
cases.stimulus_notes: Keep committed state feedback low, pulse event_intr_i from a negedge, and check that intr_o stays low on the following sampled cycle. Held-out should clear committed state first, then repeat the same check on a later event pulse.

cases.name: case129_prim_onehot_zero_enabled_suppressed
cases.bug_type: zero-hot while enabled is no longer rejected
cases.spec: With strict checking enabled, en_i high with oh_i equal to zero shall assert err_o in the same sampled cycle.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (((oh_i == 4'b0000) && ($past(oh_i) == 4'b0000) && en_i && $past(en_i))) |-> err_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: Strict onehot checking must reject the all-zero request vector while enabled.

loose_negative_controls.name: request_implies_enable
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) ((oh_i == 4'b0001) || (oh_i == 4'b0010) || (oh_i == 4'b0100) || (oh_i == 4'b1000)) |-> en_i);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It constrains only active-request cases and says nothing about enabled-zero.

loose_negative_controls.name: multihot_only
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The mutation leaves multihot detection intact and only breaks the strict zero-hot corner.

cases.hard_case_rationale: A broad 'onehot or enabled' check can still pass here. The useful assertion has to name the strict zero-hot-while-enabled corner explicitly.
cases.overfit_lure: Primary trace should include a tempting enabled-zero literal like 4'b0000 between valid onehot patterns.
cases.stimulus_notes: Drive a legal onehot first, then hold en_i high while forcing oh_i to 4'b0000. Held-out should reuse a different surrounding onehot pattern before the same strict zero-hot corner.

cases.name: case130_prim_fifo_empty_early
cases.bug_type: empty asserts one slot early
cases.spec: empty_o shall remain low while the FIFO still contains exactly one entry.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (depth_o == 3'd1) |-> !empty_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: Single-entry occupancy must not be mistaken for empty.

loose_negative_controls.name: no_full_when_empty
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) empty_o |-> !full_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The buggy FIFO can still avoid asserting full while empty_o rises too early.

loose_negative_controls.name: reads_reduce_depth
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) incr_rptr_i |-> !full_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It never checks the exact one-entry boundary where empty_o must stay low.

cases.hard_case_rationale: This is the mirror image of the classic empty-late bug: only the exact occupancy-1 boundary distinguishes correct from buggy.
cases.overfit_lure: The primary trace should visibly walk through depth 2,1,0 so literal-matching methods have a tempting shortcut.
cases.stimulus_notes: Write entries, drain down to one remaining item, and sample empty_o before the final read. Held-out should revisit the one-entry boundary after a clear pulse and refill.

cases.name: case131_prim_filter_disabled_bypass_stale_alt
cases.bug_type: disabled filter bypass stays on stored state
cases.spec: When enable_i is low, filter_o shall reflect the live filter_i input immediately rather than the stored filtered value.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!enable_i && $past(enable_i) && (filter_i != $past(filter_i)) && ($past(filter_o) == $past(filter_i))) |-> (filter_o == filter_i));
golden_sva.expected_behavior: On the first disabled sampled cycle after a previously tracked value is established, the bypassed output must follow the live input immediately.

loose_negative_controls.name: enabled_only
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (enable_i && filter_o) |-> filter_i);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It only checks cycles where the enabled path is already driving high, so it ignores the disabled bypass path entirely.

loose_negative_controls.name: steady_input_eventual_match
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (enable_i && filter_i && $past(filter_i)) |-> filter_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The filtered path can still converge correctly while the disabled bypass path remains stale.

cases.hard_case_rationale: This mutation preserves the filtered behavior and only breaks the control-path bypass. Assertions that focus on threshold behavior miss it.
cases.stimulus_notes: Build up the stored value while enabled, then disable from a negedge and flip filter_i so the first disabled sampled cycle must reflect the live input. Held-out should establish the opposite stored polarity before disabling.

cases.name: case132_prim_edge_posedge_missing
cases.bug_type: posedge pulse is dropped entirely
cases.spec: A sampled 0->1 transition shall generate a one-cycle pulse on q_posedge_pulse_o.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!$past(q_sync_o) && q_sync_o) |-> q_posedge_pulse_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: Every sampled rising edge must create a visible posedge pulse.

loose_negative_controls.name: pulse_onehot_only
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) !(q_posedge_pulse_o && q_negedge_pulse_o));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: A completely missing posedge pulse still satisfies exclusivity.

loose_negative_controls.name: negedge_path_only
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) ($past(q_sync_o) && !q_sync_o) |-> q_negedge_pulse_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The falling-edge path can remain correct while the rising-edge pulse disappears.

cases.hard_case_rationale: A generic 'there is some pulse activity' statement is too weak; the exact rise-to-pulse contract matters.
cases.stimulus_notes: Toggle d_i low-to-high between clock edges and sample the next posedge. Held-out should include a longer low dwell before the rise.

cases.name: case133_prim_edge_negedge_missing
cases.bug_type: negedge pulse is dropped entirely
cases.spec: A sampled 1->0 transition shall generate a one-cycle pulse on q_negedge_pulse_o.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) ($past(d_i) && !d_i) |-> q_negedge_pulse_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: Every sampled falling edge must create a visible negedge pulse.

loose_negative_controls.name: pulse_onehot_only
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) !(q_posedge_pulse_o && q_negedge_pulse_o));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: A missing negedge pulse still satisfies exclusivity.

loose_negative_controls.name: posedge_path_only
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!$past(q_sync_o) && q_sync_o) |-> q_posedge_pulse_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The rising-edge path can stay correct while the falling-edge pulse disappears.

cases.hard_case_rationale: Like the posedge variant, this needs the exact boundary relation rather than a vague pulse-exists check.
cases.stimulus_notes: Drive a clean high interval first, then force a falling edge between sampled clocks. Held-out should interleave extra rises between the fall checks.

cases.name: case134_prim_intr_event_not_sticky
cases.bug_type: event interrupt state drops when the source pulse goes away
cases.spec: In Event mode, a captured event shall remain latched in the interrupt state until software clears it.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) ($past(reg2hw_intr_state_q_i) && reg2hw_intr_state_q_i && reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i) |-> intr_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: Once event state is latched and remains high, the enabled interrupt output must stay asserted on the next sampled cycle.

loose_negative_controls.name: event_sets_state_next_cycle
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) event_intr_i |-> reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It checks only that the sampled hardware event arrived while enabled, not whether the interrupt stayed latched afterward.

loose_negative_controls.name: masked_interrupt_low
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i) |-> !intr_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The bug is about event retention while enabled, not masked behavior.

cases.hard_case_rationale: A momentary event makes this easy to miss with generic 'event seen' wording. The contract is specifically about retention across cycles.
cases.stimulus_notes: Pulse event_intr_i high for one cycle under enable, then keep it low without clearing state. Held-out should insert an extra idle cycle before the pulse.

cases.name: case135_prim_intr_enable_mask_ignored
cases.bug_type: interrupt output ignores the enable mask
cases.spec: Even if interrupt state is set, intr_o shall be low in any sampled cycle where reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i is low.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i && !$past(reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i) && reg2hw_intr_state_q_i && $past(reg2hw_intr_state_q_i)) |-> !intr_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: The output mask must suppress interrupt visibility immediately when enable is low.

loose_negative_controls.name: event_updates_state
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) event_intr_i |-> hw2reg_intr_state_de_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: State-update correctness says nothing about whether the mask is applied at the outgoing interrupt pin.

loose_negative_controls.name: enabled_event_visible
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i && $past(reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i) && reg2hw_intr_state_q_i && $past(reg2hw_intr_state_q_i)) |-> intr_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The buggy design still satisfies enabled visibility while failing masked suppression after enable drops.

cases.hard_case_rationale: Many loose interrupt assertions check only that enabled events become visible. The hard part is checking the exact masked corner after state has already gone high.
cases.stimulus_notes: Raise interrupt state first, then drop reg2hw_intr_enable_q_i while holding state high. Held-out should do the same after a different event prelude.

cases.name: case136_prim_filter_ctr_disabled_bypass_stale_alt
cases.bug_type: counter-based disabled filter bypass stays on stored state
cases.spec: When enable_i is low, the counter-based filter shall bypass to the current input in the same sampled cycle.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (!enable_i && $past(enable_i) && (filter_i != $past(filter_i)) && ($past(filter_o) == $past(filter_i))) |-> (filter_o == filter_i));
golden_sva.expected_behavior: On the first disabled sampled cycle after a previously tracked value is established, the counter-based bypass must follow the live input immediately.

loose_negative_controls.name: enabled_threshold_only
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (enable_i && filter_o) |-> filter_i);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: The enabled threshold path can still look fine on cycles where it is already driving high while the disabled bypass path remains stale.

loose_negative_controls.name: threshold_nonzero
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) enable_i |-> (thresh_i == thresh_i));
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It never constrains the bypass output relation at all.

cases.hard_case_rationale: This keeps the counter machinery intact and only corrupts the disabled bypass path, which is exactly the kind of bug broad filter assertions tend to miss.
cases.stimulus_notes: Accumulate the stored value while enabled, then disable from a negedge and flip filter_i so the next sampled cycle must reflect the live input. Held-out should force the opposite stored polarity before disabling.

cases.name: case137_prim_onehot_addr_false_positive
cases.bug_type: legal onehot request spuriously flags address error
cases.spec: If exactly one bit of oh_i is high and addr_i points to that bit, err_o shall remain low in the same cycle.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (((((oh_i == 4'b0001) && ($past(oh_i) == 4'b0001) && (addr_i == 2'd0) && ($past(addr_i) == 2'd0)) || ((oh_i == 4'b0010) && ($past(oh_i) == 4'b0010) && (addr_i == 2'd1) && ($past(addr_i) == 2'd1))) && en_i && $past(en_i))) |-> !err_o);
golden_sva.expected_behavior: A legal onehot/address match must not raise a spurious checker error.

loose_negative_controls.name: illegal_must_error
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) ((((oh_i == 4'b0100) && (addr_i == 2'd0)) || ((oh_i == 4'b1000) && (addr_i == 2'd1))) && en_i) |-> err_o);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It constrains only obviously illegal address mismatches and says nothing about false positives on legal requests.

loose_negative_controls.name: multihot_implies_enable
loose_negative_controls.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) ((oh_i == 4'b1010) || (oh_i == 4'b1100)) |-> en_i);
loose_negative_controls.why_it_should_miss: It only checks that an unrelated multihot stimulus was presented while enabled, so it says nothing about false positives on legal onehot requests.

cases.hard_case_rationale: This is a good negative-correctness case: generic assertions about illegal inputs still pass, but only an exact legal-corner assertion exposes the spurious error.
cases.overfit_lure: Use exact legal pairs like (4'b0001, 2'd0) and (4'b0010, 2'd1) so trace-conditioned methods are tempted to memorize the seen constants.
cases.stimulus_notes: Exercise both legal and illegal onehot/address pairs. Held-out should use a different legal bit/index match than the primary trace.
